body.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rob}}\), determine \(\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}(n,\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)\) and construct \(T_n^\star\) so that, jointly for all \(n\geq2\) and \(0\leq\epsilon\leq1/10\), \[c_0\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}\leq\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)\leq\sup_{(P,Q,R)\in\mathcal C_{d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L}(\epsilon)}\mathbb E_{R^n}|T_n^\star-\theta(P)|\leq C_0\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}.\] The rate must be an explicit finite piecewise formula with every equality-case logarithm; the estimator must be total, finite, data-only, and computationally specified; and the converse must use the same contaminated experiment. The result must decide whether the clean functional rate and \(\omega_\theta(\epsilon/(1-\epsilon))\) are simultaneously attainable or whether a quantified nuisance-contamination interaction term is unavoidable.
body.justification: This first-class open extension asks whether the simultaneous attainment proved by the one-dimensional calibration persists across the full multidimensional smoothness phase diagram.
body.gap: Section 3 of MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026 starts from clean i.i.d. observations and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 verifies its ATE trimming and boundary-bias conditions; neither allows arbitrary replacement of \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\). ChenGaoRen2016 gives generic Huber testing, and RobinsEtAl2017HOEE gives clean higher-order correction, but neither supplies the requested robust fast-functional construction and same-experiment Huber-neighborhood converse on this boundary class.
body.consumer: SasakiUra2022Robustate gains a theoretical error-radius and boundary-correction benchmark that separates limited-overlap robustness from unreliable-record robustness.
